metadata.title: Key Academic Papers and Resources on AI-Generated Text Detection and Watermarking (English Focus)
metadata.description: Curated list of most important, famous, latest (up to 2026), and influential arXiv papers, surveys, and related resources on detecting AI writing in English text, LLM watermarking, patterns/signals, and detector methods. Includes abstracts/key contributions relevant to indicators and patterns. Sources primarily arXiv, with cross-references to HF/GitHub where implementations appear.
metadata.selection_criteria: Fame/impact (citations, adoption), recency (latest methods/surveys), direct relevance to English text patterns (perplexity, burstiness, green list, GLTR, curvature, ML), coverage of black-box/watermark/commercial implications. Self-reviewed for comprehensiveness across categories.

key_papers.title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
key_papers.authors: John Kirchenbauer, Jonas Geiping, Yuxin Wen, Jonathan Katz, Ian Miers, Tom Goldstein
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Introduces the green list / red list watermarking mechanism. Details how to embed statistical mark during generation via logit bias on green tokens (hash-seeded partition). Provides z-score detection algorithm with theoretical bounds, high TPR at negligible FPR, robustness analysis to edits. Primary reference for 'green list' (green box related) embedded marks in English LLMs.
key_papers.relevance: Foundational for active/provenance-based detection. Explains one of the most discussed 'marks' in AI text.

key_papers.title: DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature
key_papers.authors: Eric Mitchell, Yoonho Lee, Alexander Khazatsky, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Identifies that LLM-generated text occupies negative curvature regions in log-probability function. Proposes curvature-based criterion using perturbations (e.g. T5) to detect without training data or watermark. Improves AUROC significantly over prior zero-shot (e.g. 0.95 vs 0.81). Discusses white-box access but inspires black-box approximations.
key_papers.relevance: Core paper for modern zero-shot methods and curvature as a key pattern/signal beyond simple perplexity.

key_papers.title: Fast-DetectGPT: Efficient Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text via Conditional Probability Curvature
key_papers.authors: Guangsheng Bao, Yanbin Zhao, Zhiyang Teng, Linyi Yang, Yue Zhang
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Optimizes DetectGPT by replacing expensive perturbations with efficient sampling. Achieves ~75% relative improvement in white- and black-box settings and 340x speedup. Explicitly addresses black-box scenarios. Strengthens curvature as practical signal.
key_papers.relevance: Makes zero-shot curvature detection practical; important for black-box patterns and efficiency.

key_papers.title: A Survey on LLM-Generated Text Detection: Necessity, Methods, and Future Directions
key_papers.authors: Junchao Wu, Shu Yang, Runzhe Zhan, Yulin Yuan, Derek F. Wong, Lidia S. Chao
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Classifies detection into passive (statistics-based like PPL/burstiness/stylometry, ML-based) vs active (watermarking, semantic retrieval). Reviews necessity (misinfo, academic integrity, IP), methods, datasets (HC3, MGTBench etc.), robustness issues, future directions (better generalization, adversarial robustness, multi-modal). Essential for understanding full landscape of patterns and tools.
key_papers.relevance: Best single resource to map all patterns, black-box vs others, commercial implications, and research gaps. Updated version reflects 2025 state.

key_papers.title: AI-generated Text Detection with a GLTR-based Approach
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Builds on GLTR visual tool (green/yellow/red/purple highlights based on GPT-2 ranks). Proposes pipeline combining GLTR color stats with GPT-2 predictions for binary classification (English and Spanish). Shows humans improve with GLTR viz; automates for better accuracy. Addresses limitations of pure visual.
key_papers.relevance: Directly extends the 'green box' visual mark concept into modern ML pipelines; important for explainable detection.

key_papers.title: Diversity Boosts AI-Generated Text Detection (DivEye)
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Proposes DivEye framework capturing fluctuations in unpredictability (surprisal) across text for better detection. Achieves high AUROC (up to 0.99 in some domains) on MAGE benchmark, outperforming prior methods. Emphasizes diversity/variation signals (related to burstiness but more nuanced).
key_papers.relevance: Example of latest (2026 pub) advancements focusing on refined statistical patterns for robustness across domains.

key_papers.title: AI Generated Text Detection (evaluation paper)
key_papers.key_contributions_to_indicators: Evaluates traditional ML (TF-IDF + LR) vs deep (BiLSTM, DistilBERT) on AI detection. Shows contextual models (DistilBERT) superior (88%+ acc, 0.96 ROC-AUC). Highlights importance of proper evaluation protocols to avoid topic memorization. Useful baselines for English text.
key_papers.relevance: Recent practical evaluation confirming value of transformer-based ML patterns while noting limitations.

other_resources.wikipedia: No dedicated comprehensive page on 'AI-generated text detection' or 'LLM watermarking' as of 2026 searches. Related coverage exists fragmented in 'Generative artificial intelligence', 'ChatGPT', 'Academic integrity', 'Plagiarism', or 'Large language model' pages. Academic literature (arXiv surveys) is far more authoritative and up-to-date than Wikipedia for this technical topic.
other_resources.huggingface: Rich ecosystem of fine-tuned detectors (RoBERTa variants listed in detectors_tools.json). Model cards often reference training datasets (e.g. RAID, custom human/AI pairs) and provide inference examples. Spaces for demos. Key for open-source practical deployment of ML pattern-based detectors.
other_resources.github: Implementations of GLTR, DetectGPT/Fast-DetectGPT, watermark detectors, benchmark suites (MGTBench etc.), attack tools. Essential for reproducing patterns and building custom solutions. Search terms: 'ai text detector', 'llm watermark', 'detectgpt', 'gltr'.
other_resources.datasets_mentioned: HC3 (Human vs ChatGPT), MGTBench, RAID (for robust detection), custom paired corpora in papers. Critical for training/eval of ML pattern detectors.

self_review_completeness: Selected papers represent the most cited/famous (Kirchenbauer, DetectGPT, Survey), latest advancements (2025-2026), and cover all requested angles (watermark/green list, GLTR/green box, black-box/zero-shot, patterns like curvature/PPL, ML). Iterated searches confirmed these as core. No major omissions in influential English-focused works. Classification by type aids navigation.
